docs.t: CHECK AIRMAN SCENARIO: On a post-arrival disinsection, a cargo smoke warning triggers three minutes into the 5-minute saturation period. Ten minutes after the crew is cleared to disembark, a lavatory smoke warning triggers. How do you treat each warning?
docs.x: CHECK AIRMAN SCENARIO: On a post-arrival disinsection, a cargo smoke warning triggers three minutes into the 5-minute saturation period. Ten minutes after the crew is cleared to disembark, a lavatory smoke warning triggers. How do you treat each warning? The warning during the saturation period is spurious: from the start of spraying until the clearance to disembark is given (including the 5-minute saturation time), lavatory or cargo smoke warnings are treated as spurious. The warning ten minutes after disembark clearance falls outside that window, so it is treated as real and the crew follows the associated procedure. From the start of spraying until the clearance to disembark is given (including 5-minute saturation time), any lavatory or cargo smoke warnings during this period should be treated as spurious. However, if any smoke warnings trigger outside those times, the crew should follow the associated procedure.
